newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cemex Spanish unit gets $850 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Cemex Spanish unit gets $850 mln loan.

text.p: Valenciana de Cementos, the Spanish subsidiary of Mexico-based cement giant Cemex S.A., has obtained a syndicated loan worth $850 million, Cemex said.
The loan, denominated in several currencies, has a maturity of seven years and will be used to refinance existing debt at Valenciana, Cemex said.
The loan, the biggest ever negotiated by a Spanish company, will also be used to refinance debt at other parts of Cemex S.A. through inter-company transactions, the company said.

"The success of the syndicated loan shows the confidence that financial institutions have in Cemex's financial strategy. The high level of demand by the banks forced us to assign it on a pro rata basis," Rodrigo Trevino, corporate finance director, said in the statement.
The loan was negotiated by the following banks: Argentaria Banco de Negocios, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya, Citibank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, J.P Morgan and Chase Manhattan.
Cemex is the world's third largest cement producer, with operations in Mexico, Spain, the United States, Venezuela, Colombia and Panama.
